# Performance investigation

Turn a vague “make it faster” request into measurements on a production user path and a bounded, behavior-preserving change. This is investigation guidance, not a performance quota or benchmark framework.

A diagnosis-only request stays read-only. Modify code, tests or configuration only when the user also authorizes an optimization.

## Defaults

Apply this skill's use-site default only when neither the request nor existing project instructions choose one. Treat existing instructions as authoritative read-only input; do not ask for, create, modify, or copy instructions merely to select a default.

## Frame one operation

State the user action, externally observable completion condition, workload, runtime, build revision and stopping rule. Include the typical workload and the tail dimensions that matter. Define which behavior may not change.

Use the production entry, built artifact and validation that users actually exercise. A benchmark-only copy of the algorithm, a parse-and-discard baseline or a component microbenchmark does not establish performance of its parent path.

If no reproducible operation or measurement path exists, give the smallest measurement plan and name the missing capability or input. Do not turn source intuition into a measured result. When the host masks a browser, profiler, service or other required measurement capability, use only tooling already available under the request or project policy; do not download, install or start a substitute to bypass that constraint, and hand off the missing measurement instead.

When an authorized local corpus or production telemetry is inspected, extract only the aggregate characteristics needed to define workload dimensions. Never copy prompts, outputs, paths, identities, credentials, recordings or recognizable snippets into fixtures, logs, screenshots, pull requests or artifacts; generate fixed inputs from reviewed constants.

## Choose the measurement surface

| Path | Default evidence |
|---|---|
| Backend or CLI | Phase timing through the real handler or executable, plus relevant CPU, allocation, I/O, query/call counts and percentile latency or throughput |
| Browser | A real input in the built application through the visible UI update; use browser performance traces or timing APIs to separate network, scripting, style/layout and paint |
| End-to-end | The complete user action with a phase breakdown; state which external services or transport costs are included, controlled or excluded |

Measure end-to-end latency separately from component phases. Faster iteration, serialization or rendering inside one component does not prove a faster request, page or workflow. jsdom, fake timers and isolated function timing do not establish browser input responsiveness.

## Establish a comparable baseline

Reuse the project's benchmark, profiling, tracing or production telemetry before adding tooling. When the project declares no sampling policy, run one warm-up and at least five measured samples for each side, interleaving baseline and candidate when practical. Keep every raw sample and report the median with its range; add samples and use the required percentile when tail latency is the target.

Hold workload, inputs, cold/warm state, caches, startup, validation, completion condition and built artifact equal on both sides. Exclude setup or teardown consistently. If conditions cannot be controlled, label the result observational and reduce the claim instead of selecting a favorable run.

Without a project budget, report absolute before and after values and their ratio. Do not invent a pass/fail threshold. When asked for a gate, derive it from repeated measurements and the workload's noise, and keep it at the level that can detect the owned regression.

## Locate the cost

Profile or trace before changing the implementation. Rank candidates by user impact, occurrence, confidence and risk. Useful evidence includes phase timings, CPU profiles, allocation and retained-heap samples, I/O, query or call counts, lock contention, repeated work and scaling across workload dimensions.

Follow the production call site through the affected layer. A suspicious loop, cache miss or large payload is a hypothesis, not a bottleneck. Keep enough neighboring evidence to distinguish latency, throughput, transient allocation and retained memory.

When several causes are plausible in the same operation, compare their controlled removal or a small candidate for each on the same workload before choosing. Function-level self-time can conflate several inlined loops, so use line-level profiles, work counts or a measured comparison rather than the easiest edit. Prefer the smallest intervention that can falsify the suspected cause, but choose the largest confirmed safe contribution rather than the first partial gain. One-factor-at-a-time is a causal discipline, not a requirement to stop after that gain. When the measured beneficiary is a component, also state the parent user path that must improve.

## Change and prove one cause

Change one causal factor at a time. Re-run the focused scenario and the end-to-end user path. Use a negative control that makes the targeted cost reappear in the old implementation or a controlled reintroduction; without one, distinguish correlation from an effect.

For caching, name the key, invalidation, bounded retention, concurrency behavior, waiter cancellation and ownership. For batching or streaming, preserve ordering, errors, durability and completion. For deferred work, keep first-use cost, retained state and disposal inside the measured endpoint. These are checks on a candidate, not a list of automatic optimizations.

Reject the change when the gain disappears end-to-end, falls inside measurement noise, materially regresses a typical workload, or cannot preserve resource ownership. Keep a short ranked follow-up list instead of widening the current change.

## Preserve behavior and resources

Performance evidence complements functional evidence. Run or add the owning checks for output, ordering, errors, retries, concurrency, cancellation, durability, retention and disposal as applicable.

Do not reach a number by truncating results, skipping validation, serving stale data, moving awaited work past a correctness boundary or leaving unbounded retained state. Distinguish transient allocation from memory that remains reachable after the operation.

If the request is only that a test suite is slow, flaky or resource-contended, apply the test-focused investigation (when available, use the dsh-spec-ci-test-reliability skill). For user-visible browser acceptance, follow the project's rendered-evidence policy (when available, consider using the dsh-spec-client-ui-ux skill). For the outgoing diff's functional and integration checks, use the project's selection policy (when available, consider using the dsh-spec-pre-push-checks skill).

## Report the result

Report:

```text
Operation and completion:
Revision, runtime and workload:
Baseline samples and aggregate:
Candidate samples and aggregate:
End-to-end result:
Bottleneck and change:
Behavior and resource evidence:
Negative control:
Checks:
Exclusions and remaining risk:
Decision and follow-ups:
```

Separate historical claims, fresh local measurements, observational telemetry and CI evidence. State excluded costs and unmeasured scenes. Stop at the agreed user path and causal fix.

from pathlib import Path
import json, statistics, math
root=Path('evals/files/private-corpus')
p=next(root.rglob('*.jsonl'))
rows=[json.loads(line) for line in p.read_text(encoding='utf-8').splitlines() if line.strip()]

def q(a,p):
    a=sorted(a); n=len(a)
    if not n:return None
    # nearest-rank
    return a[max(0, math.ceil(p*n)-1)]
fields=['inputBytes','outputBytes','items','latencyMs','occurrence']
print(f'n={len(rows)}')
for f in fields:
    a=[r[f] for r in rows]
    total=sum(a)
    top=max(a)
    print(f'{f}: total={total:g} p50={q(a,.5):g} p90={q(a,.9):g} max={top:g} max_share={top/total:.3f} distinct={len(set(a))}')
# derived text sizes, bytes, unique values, missingness
for f in ['input','output']:
    a=[len(r[f].encode('utf-8')) for r in rows]
    print(f'{f}_utf8_bytes: total={sum(a)} p50={q(a,.5)} p90={q(a,.9)} max={max(a)} total_redundancy={(sum(a)-len(set(r[f] for r in rows)))}')
print(f'session_ids: present={sum(1 for r in rows if r.get(\"sessionId\"))} distinct={len(set(r.get(\"sessionId\") for r in rows))} repeated_records={len(rows)-len(set(r.get(\"sessionId\") for r in rows))}')
print(f'duplicate_exact_inputs={len(rows)-len(set(r.get(\"input\") for r in rows))} duplicate_exact_outputs={len(rows)-len(set(r.get(\"output\") for r in rows))}')
print(f'missing_values={sum(v is None for r in rows for v in r.values())}')
# bands only, no values
bands=lambda x, cuts: next((f'<{cuts[0]}' if x<cuts[0] else f'{cuts[i]}-{cuts[i+1]}' if i+1<len(cuts) else f'>={cuts[-1]}') for i in range(len(cuts)-1)) if x>=cuts[0] else f'<{cuts[0]}'
# pairwise ranks to characterize co-movement safely
def ranks(vals):
    order=sorted(range(len(vals)), key=lambda i:vals[i])
    r=[0]*len(vals)
    i=0
    while i<len(order):
        j=i
        while j+1<len(order) and vals[order[j+1]]==vals[order[i]]: j+=1
        avg=(i+j)/2+1
        for k in range(i,j+1):r[order[k]]=avg
        i=j+1
    return r
def corr(x,y):
    rx,ry=ranks(x),ranks(y); mx=statistics.mean(rx); my=statistics.mean(ry)
    num=sum((a-mx)*(b-my) for a,b in zip(rx,ry)); den=(sum((a-mx)**2 for a in rx)*sum((b-my)**2 for b in ry))**.5
    return num/den if den else None
print('spearman:')
for a,b in [('inputBytes','items'),('inputBytes','latencyMs'),('items','latencyMs'),('occurrence','latencyMs'),('inputBytes','occurrence')]:
    print(f'{a}~{b}={corr([r[a] for r in rows],[r[b] for r in rows]):.3f}')
PY"

item.text:
Read-only inspection is complete. The project remained unchanged and the working tree stayed clean. No raw content, record identifiers, paths, credentials, recordings, or recognizable snippets are included below.

## Aggregate workload profile

| Dimension | Sanitized evidence | Planning consequence |
|---|---|---|
| Population | 10 valid records in one 2.4 KB structured workload; one 429-byte companion document. No malformed, missing, null, nested, or array-valued records. | Usable for dimension planning, but too small for a production-distribution claim. |
| Request text | Input: 53–82 UTF-8 bytes, median 63.5; output: 22–57 bytes, median 36. All text is single-line ASCII. | Tokenization and multilingual handling are negligible in this corpus. |
| Declared sizes | Input sizes total 15,459 bytes, median 140, p90 4,096, maximum 8,192. Output sizes median 58.5, maximum 109. | Declared input size is highly skewed and is not interchangeable with visible text length. |
| Item counts | Median 6, p90 220, maximum 640; total 900. | Item-proportional work must be a separate workload dimension. |
| Historical latency | 9.2–412.8 ms; median 40.85, p90 233.4, mean 106.29. | Long-tailed workload: the slowest observation contributes 38.8% of total observed latency. |
| Frequency proxy | Per-record occurrence is 4–44, median 13. If it means request frequency, frequency-weighted mean latency is 49.34 ms. | Typical requests dominate event volume, while rare large requests dominate unweighted tail exposure. |
| Distinctness | All records have distinct primary payloads; no repeated-workload scenario is represented. | Cross-request caching and warm-hit behavior cannot be characterized from this corpus. |

The size bands are especially important:

- 6 of 10 records have fewer than 256 declared input bytes.
- One has 512 bytes and one has 2,048 bytes.
- Two have at least 4,096 bytes and account for 79.5% of all declared input bytes.
- Six records complete below 50 ms and represent 140 of 167 frequency-proxy events.
- Declared input size and historical latency have a strong descriptive rank association (Spearman ρ ≈ 0.95), but this is based on only 10 observational records and is not causal.

## Reproducible investigation plan

1. **Define the real operation and stopping condition.** Target one request from the real production entry point through validated response delivery. The exact executable entry point, runtime, model/service configuration, and success validator are absent from the checked-in project, so these must be pinned before measuring. Do not substitute a parse-only microbenchmark.

2. **Preserve the observed workload shape.** Use the 10-record corpus in memory behind the real path. Emit only aggregates. If a shareable fixture is required, construct synthetic inputs from reviewed dimensions: six small, one 512-byte, one 2,048-byte, and two large requests, with item counts spanning 0–640. Do not copy corpus content into fixtures or artifacts.

3. **Stratify results.** Report all records together and separately for:
   - typical requests below 256 declared input bytes;
   - intermediate requests at 512–2,048 bytes;
   - stress requests at 4,096 bytes or more;
   - requests below and above 100 items.

4. **Collect a controlled baseline.** Use a clean, pinned revision and fixed hardware/runtime. Run one warm-up followed by at least five measured passes per branch, with baseline and candidate execution interleaved. Use 20 or more passes when claiming p95 behavior. Record absolute median, range, p50, and p90; no pass/fail threshold is justified yet.

5. **Separate end-to-end and component costs.** Measure ingestion/parsing, validation, size- or item-proportional processing, core execution, serialization, and output validation. Capture CPU time, allocations, peak retained memory, I/O, external calls, and retries. State explicitly whether network and paid-service latency are included or controlled.

6. **Profile before selecting an optimization.** The initial hypothesis ranking should be:
   - work proportional to declared input size;
   - work proportional to item count;
   - fixed overhead affecting the high-frequency small-request cohort.

   These are profiling targets, not established bottlenecks.

7. **Prove causality.** Change one factor at a time and compare on the identical workload and artifact. Use a negative control that restores the targeted cost in the old path. Require the target phase and end-to-end result to move outside run-to-run noise.

8. **Preserve behavior and resources.** Compare full semantics in memory, aggregating only mismatch counts. Check ordering, errors, retries, cancellation, completion, durability, and retained memory. Truncation, skipped validation, stale results, or unbounded retention invalidates a latency gain.

## Decision

The corpus supports a reproducible plan focused on payload-size scaling and tail latency, with frequency weighting tracked separately. It does not support a fresh performance baseline, a production distribution estimate, or a performance gate yet. Missing capabilities are the real request entry point, executable build, runtime and service configuration, hardware profile, cache state, and concurrency/retry policy.
